proposal_backlog.title: Public release readiness pass
proposal_backlog.rationale: The repo is intended to become public, so Lambchop should verify public-facing docs, privacy scans, install instructions, and dashboard onboarding before wider use.
suggested_acceptance_criteria: README gives a concise public install path.
Privacy and secret scans are documented as a release gate.
Dashboard hub/API setup is understandable from a fresh checkout.
proposal_backlog.risk_notes: Requires user approval because public release scope and acceptable history-scrubbing depth are product decisions.
proposal_backlog.parallelization_notes: Can split into docs polish, validation gate, and dashboard onboarding tasks.

proposal_backlog.title: Target repo upgrade fixture and proof
proposal_backlog.rationale: Lambchop now supports upgrading existing installs; a reusable fixture would prove the migration path without touching private projects.
suggested_acceptance_criteria: A fixture simulates an older Lambchop install.
Upgrade steps preserve history while adding proposal backlog and dashboard API fields.
Validation evidence is recorded in progress.
proposal_backlog.risk_notes: Fixture design should avoid embedding any private repo details.
proposal_backlog.parallelization_notes: Can split into fixture creation, migration validation, and docs update.

proposal_backlog.title: Dashboard proposal review visibility
proposal_backlog.rationale: Proposal backlog entries should be visible where the user monitors automation status, so review-needed work does not hide in JSON.
suggested_acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows proposal title, rationale, status, and review need.
Status API returns proposal_backlog from state or dashboard data.
Empty proposal state is clearly rendered.
proposal_backlog.risk_notes: Approval actions should remain manual for now; the dashboard should not mutate project state.
proposal_backlog.parallelization_notes: Small UI/API task, likely single-lane unless paired with docs.

lambchop_source.notes: Self-maintenance ledger records the applied feature commit. Target repos record the external Lambchop source commit used during setup/upgrade and compare it with current Lambchop source during future check-ins.
